newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: China police act against Uighur businesswoman - friend.
newsitem.headline: China police act against Uighur businesswoman - friend.

text.p: Chinese police have prevented a prominent ethnic Uighur businesswoman flying to neighbouring Kazakhstan, a friend said on Saturday.
Khabiba Yesenova told Reuters in the Kazakh capital Almaty that police had intervened when Robiya Kodir was about to board a plane in the Xinjiang provincial capital, Urumqi, on Friday.
The province has been the scene of recent unrest in support of autonomy demands by the Turkic Uighur people.
"She could only call her (Almaty) friends on the telephone to say that police had taken away her passport and told her she no longer had the right to travel abroad," Yesenova said.
Yesenova could not say why any travel ban was imposed on Kodir, whose husband currently lives in the United States where he campaigns for Xinjiang's independence.
But she suggested that Kodir, one of the richest and most popular people in Xinjiang, had been barred from leaving China for her support for Uighur separatists.
"She has always been with her people," Yesenova said. "She was in the town of Yining during the riot of local Uighurs in February," Yesenova said.

In February, Yining, near China's border border with Kazakhstan, was shattered by one of the largest demonstrations for independence in Xinjiang since the 1949 communist takeover. The riot left nine people dead and 198 wounded.

Beijing said the riot had erupted after local separatists prevented police arrested Uighurs on criminal charges. Uighurs accuse Beijing of discrimination, forced assimilation and mass executions of their leaders.
